question: Distinguish between capital expenditure and revenue expenditure, with an example of each.
sources: Standard accounting principles: distinction between capital and revenue expenditure
AS 10, Property, Plant and Equipment (issued by ICAI) - recognition of cost

points.label: Capital expenditure
points.description: Gives a benefit over more than one accounting period: acquires or improves fixed assets, or increases earning capacity.
points.basis: AS 10, recognition of an item of property, plant and equipment; accounting principle of capital expenditure

points.label: Revenue expenditure
points.description: Benefit is consumed within the accounting period: maintains day-to-day operations or existing earning capacity.
points.basis: Accounting principle of revenue expenditure; matching concept

points.label: Accounting treatment
points.description: Capital expenditure is shown as an asset in the balance sheet (and depreciated); revenue expenditure is charged to the profit and loss account.
points.basis: AS 10 (day-to-day servicing costs are recognised in profit or loss; asset carried at cost less depreciation); matching concept

points.label: Examples
points.description: Capital: purchase of machinery or extension of a building. Revenue: repairs, wages, rent.
points.basis: Accounting principle: examples of capital and revenue expenditure
